source_spans.quote: For purposes of this chapter, minor applicants are defined as un-emancipated applicants under the age of 18.

claim_judgments.rationale: C0000 correctly reflects U0001 defining minor applicants as un-emancipated applicants under the age of 18 for the purposes of this chapter. Scope, summary, boundary, and actor are properly aligned.

source_spans.quote: The applicant must explain any material discrepancies between the name on the application and the name recorded in the evidence of U.S. citizenship/non-citizen U.S. nationality and the evidence of identity (see 22 CFR 51.25).

claim_judgments.rationale: C0001 captures the requirement for the applicant to explain material discrepancies between the name on the application and evidence of citizenship/nationality and identity under 22 CFR 51.25, accurately matching U0003.

source_spans.quote: Evidence of material name changes must be reviewed for evidence of counterfeiting or alteration (see 8 FAM 201.1)

claim_judgments.rationale: C0002 accurately conveys that evidence of material name changes must be reviewed for evidence of counterfeiting or alteration as specified in U0010.

source_spans.quote: The applicant may not continue to use a previous name after a material name change unless the name change documentation specifically permits the applicant to continue using that name (see 8 FAM 403.1-6 regarding “known as” names).

claim_judgments.rationale: C0003 correctly summarizes the prohibition that an applicant may not continue using a previous name after a material name change unless specifically permitted by the documentation, matching U0011.

source_spans.quote: unless the name change documentation specifically permits the applicant to continue using that name

claim_judgments.rationale: C0004 isolates the exception clause of U0011/C0003 and correctly reflects that an applicant may continue using a previous name if the documentation specifically permits doing so.

source_spans.quote: If the applicant has had a material name change more than one year prior to applying on form DS-11 but has not updated her/his ID to reflect the material name change, you must suspend the application to request an acceptable ID in the new name.

claim_judgments.rationale: C0005 accurately represents the requirement to suspend the application to request acceptable ID in the new name if the name change occurred more than one year prior to applying on form DS-11 and ID was not updated, completely covering U0013.

source_spans.quote: If the applicant has had a material name change more than one year prior to applying on form DS-11 but has not updated her/his ID to reflect the material name change, you must suspend the application to request an acceptable ID in the new name. If there is insufficient time to request that the applicant submit acceptable ID prior to urgent or emergency travel, a limited-validity passport may be issued in the requested name;

claim_judgments.rationale: C0006 captures the permission to issue a limited-validity passport in the requested name when there is insufficient time before urgent or emergency travel to request updated ID from an applicant who changed their name more than a year prior on form DS-11, covering U0014.

source_spans.quote: You must fully notate the name change documentation prior to returning the documentation, including that the documentation was "seen and returned," to the applicant with the information request letter (IRL);

claim_judgments.rationale: C0007 accurately reflects the requirement to fully notate name change documentation (including 'seen and returned') prior to returning it with an IRL, corresponding to U0016.

source_spans.quote: Applicants who have had a material name change within one year of applying on a form DS-11 do not need to submit ID in the new name.

claim_judgments.rationale: C0008 properly represents the exemption stating that applicants with a material name change within one year of applying on form DS-11 do not need to submit ID in the new name, fulfilling U0017.

source_spans.quote: Applicants who have had a material name change within one year of applying on a form DS-11 do not need to submit ID in the new name. However, if the ID has not yet been changed, they must submit their name change documentation.

claim_judgments.rationale: C0009 correctly states the condition and requirement that if ID has not yet been changed for applicants who changed names within one year on DS-11, they must submit their name change documentation, covering U0018.

source_spans.quote: The court order or decree must be final:

claim_judgments.rationale: C0010 correctly captures the requirement that a court order or decree must be final, aligning with U0019.

source_spans.quote: An applicant with a pending name change must not be issued a passport in her/his new name.

claim_judgments.rationale: The draft claim accurately reflects the source prohibition that an applicant with a pending name change must not be issued a passport in their new name.

source_spans.quote: An applicant with a pending name change must not be issued a form FS-240 in her/his new name.

claim_judgments.rationale: The claim accurately reflects the rule prohibiting issuance of a Form FS-240 in a new name to an applicant with a pending name change.

source_spans.quote: You must clear the applicant's pending name even though the name change is not final and even if the passport is not being issued at this time.

claim_judgments.rationale: The claim correctly states the adjudicator's duty to clear the pending name regardless of finality or immediate issuance.

source_spans.quote: The court order or decree must list both the applicant's current and former name(s).

claim_judgments.rationale: The claim accurately captures the mandatory requirement that a court order or decree list both current and former names.

source_spans.quote: When this occurs, the applicant must provide both her/his current and former names on the application.

claim_judgments.rationale: The claim accurately states the obligation for the applicant to provide both current and former names on the application when former name confidentiality applies.

source_spans.quote: You may request additional evidence of U.S. citizenship/non-citizen U.S. nationality or identity in accordance with 22 CFR 51.23 and 22 CFR 51.45.

claim_judgments.rationale: The claim correctly details the adjudicator's authority to request additional evidence of citizenship/nationality or identity when processing a confidential former name order.

source_spans.quote: if the applicant has a name with multiple parts, you must determine how the name will appear:

claim_judgments.rationale: The claim accurately captures the requirement that an adjudicator determine how a multi-part name will appear.

source_spans.quote: If the applicant's previous passport had a space, you should add a space on the current application;

claim_judgments.rationale: The claim accurately captures the recommendation to add a space if the previous passport had a space.

source_spans.quote: If the applicant does not have a previous passport and the applicant's evidence of U.S. citizenship/non-citizen U.S. nationality or ID has a space, you should add a space on the current application;

claim_judgments.rationale: The claim accurately captures the recommendation to add a space for an applicant lacking a previous passport when their citizenship evidence or ID contains a space.

source_spans.quote: If the applicant expresses a clear preference to add or remove space, either verbally or in writing, you may add or remove it per the applicant's preference.

claim_judgments.rationale: The claim correctly reflects the permission to add or remove space according to an applicant's expressed preference.

source_spans.quote: If you receive applications from several family members, you should space the last names consistently, unless a family member expresses a clear preference for a different spacing.

claim_judgments.rationale: The claim accurately captures the recommendation for consistent spacing across family members' applications unless a clear preference is expressed.

claim_judgments.rationale: The claim accurately captures the recommendation for matching last name spacing to the sponsor on special-issuance passports.
